title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE USE OF AGRICULTURAL CHEMICALS, ESTABLISHING BUFFER ZONES AROUND COMMERCIAL PLANTATIONS, PROHIBITING AERIAL SPRAYING, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Agriculture and Food, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Agricultural Chemical Regulation and Buffer Zone Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause.

sections.text:
Pursuant to Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, the City Government of Davao shall ensure and support the promotion of health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, and preserve the comfort and convenience of its inhabitants.

It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to regulate the application of agricultural chemicals in commercial crop plantations and farmlands in order to protect residential communities, schools, and water sources from the hazards of chemical drift, while supporting sustainable agricultural productivity across the city.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of general welfare powers under RA 7160 §16.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitional section modeled after Ord. 0309-07 and Ord. 0897-22.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall apply to all commercial plantations, agricultural corporate farms, agricultural landowners, farm operators, and spraying contractors operating within the territorial jurisdiction of the City of Davao.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard scope and coverage clause.

sections.text:
All owners, operators, and managers of commercial agricultural plantations within Davao City shall establish and maintain a mandatory thirty (30) meter buffer zone along the perimeter boundary of their plantations adjacent to residential zones, schools, public roads, and natural water bodies.

The buffer zone must be planted with appropriate trees, bamboo, and tall vegetative barriers capable of minimizing and intercepting chemical drift from field operations. Plantations shall be given a period of six (6) months from the effectivity of this Ordinance to fully establish compliant buffer zones.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal land use setback regulation modeled after Ord. 0309-07 §6.

sections.text:
Aerial spraying shall be strictly prohibited in all agricultural activities and commercial crop plantations within the territorial jurisdiction of Davao City after a three (3) month transition period from the effectivity of this Ordinance.

All agricultural entities and plantation operators currently employing aerial spraying shall shift to ground-based application methods. Any person or entity found applying or causing the application of agricultural chemicals through aerial spraying shall be subject to the penalties provided in this Ordinance.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Presidential Decree No. 1144 §6; Presidential Decree No. 1144 §8
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Presidential Decree No. 1144 §§6 and 8, which vest exclusive national regulatory and licensing authority over pesticide application methods in the Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority (FPA). Struck down in Mosqueda v. PBGEA (2016) under the Magtajas preemption doctrine.

sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §16; Presidential Decree No. 856
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local safety standards promoting agricultural worker health.

sections.text:
The City Agriculturist's Office (CAO), in coordination with the City Environment and Natural Resources Office (City ENRO) and the City Health Office (CHO), shall be the primary implementing agencies of this Ordinance.

The implementing offices shall conduct periodic inspections of commercial plantations, verify the establishment of required buffer zones, investigate community complaints regarding chemical drift, and submit regular compliance reports to the City Mayor and the Sangguniang Panlungsod.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard institutional implementation clause assigning duties to CAO, CENRO, and CHO.

sections.text:
Upon discovery of any violation of Section 5 or Section 7 of this Ordinance, the City Agriculturist's Office shall immediately issue a written Notice of Violation directing the owner or operator of the plantation to institute corrective measures within fifteen (15) working days.

Failure to rectify the violation within the prescribed period shall result in the filing of appropriate administrative and judicial charges against the non-compliant entity.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard administrative enforcement notice modeled after Ord. 0495-21 and Ord. 0354-23.

sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Strictly complies with the statutory penalty ceiling of P5,000 fine and 1-year imprisonment under RA 7160 §458.

sections.text: If, for any reason, any section or provision of this Ordinance is declared unconstitutional or invalid, other sections or provisions hereof not affected thereby shall continue to be in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its complete publication in a newspaper of general circulation in the City of Davao.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE ENHANCING PUBLIC SAFETY AND SECURITY MEASURES IN OVERLAND TRANSPORT TERMINALS, MANDATING PASSENGER AND BAGGAGE SCREENING, PRESCRIBING TERMINAL REGULATIONS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Transportation and Communication, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Overland Transport Terminal Safety and Security Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause.

sections.text:
Under Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), the City Government of Davao is authorized to exercise powers essential to the promotion of general welfare, maintenance of peace and order, and protection of public safety.

It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to promote the safety, comfort, and security of passengers, commuters, and transport workers using overland transport terminals by establishing comprehensive security standards and regulating terminal operations throughout the city.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of general welfare powers under RA 7160 §16.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitions modeled after Ord. 048-22 and Ord. 000102-03.

sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of local police powers regulating terminal safety infrastructure.

sections.text:
In the interest of public safety and crime prevention, security personnel, terminal marshals, and law enforcement officers deployed at terminal checkpoints are authorized to stop and conduct thorough physical inspections of all motor vehicles, delivery vans, and private conveyances entering or utilizing terminal staging areas, including opening and inspecting luggage compartments, trunks, and enclosed cargo spaces, and to seize any unauthorized or suspicious articles found therein.

Any driver, owner, or passenger who refuses to permit the opening and inspection of vehicle compartments shall be denied entry, held for police investigation, and cited for an ordinance violation.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: 1987 Constitution, Art. III §2; Republic Act No. 4136 §5
sections.legal_rationale: Violates Article III, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution (guarantee against unreasonable searches and seizures) and RA 4136. Routine administrative entry into public terminals permits visual exterior checkpoints, but local ordinances cannot authorize mandatory warrantless interior searches, trunk inspections, and detention without judicial warrants or probable cause.

sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Presidential Decree No. 856; Batas Pambansa Blg. 344
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local sanitation and accessibility standards under national public health and accessibility laws.

sections.text:
The City Transport and Traffic Management Office (CTTMO) shall formulate and enforce traffic routing, loading and unloading schedules, and designated vehicle bays within and surrounding all terminal premises.

No public utility vehicle shall pick up or drop passengers along public streets or thoroughfares within one hundred (100) meters of any terminal entrance or exit gate, except at designated CTTMO passenger stops.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal authority regulating vehicular traffic routing under RA 7160.

sections.text:
The Public Safety and Security Office (PSSO), in coordination with the City Transport and Traffic Management Office (CTTMO) and the Davao City Police Office (DCPO), shall oversee the implementation and enforcement of this Ordinance.

Said agencies shall conduct regular safety audits of transport terminals and ensure that security standards and passenger protections are strictly observed.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard implementing agency clause assigning duties to PSSO, CTTMO, and DCPO.

sections.text:
Whenever a terminal operator fails to maintain required screening equipment or sanitary standards, the PSSO shall issue a written Notice of Deficiency requiring the operator to rectify the deficiency within ten (10) calendar days from receipt thereof.

Failure to comply with the directive within the prescribed period shall subject the operator to the penalties herein provided.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard administrative enforcement notice clause.

sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Complies strictly with the statutory penalty bounds under RA 7160 §458.

sections.text: If any provision or part of this Ordinance is declared invalid or unconstitutional by a competent court, the remaining provisions not affected thereby shall continue in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days following its complete publication in a newspaper of local circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING INDUSTRIAL AIR EMISSIONS, MANDATING POLLUTION CONTROL MEASURES IN MANUFACTURING AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENTS, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Environment and Natural Resources, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Industrial Air Quality and Emission Regulation Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause.

sections.text:
In accordance with Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), local government units are mandated to enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology and promote public health and safety.

It is hereby declared the policy of the City Government of Davao to maintain clean air and regulate stationary sources of air pollution, ensuring that industrial and commercial operations do not discharge harmful smoke, fumes, or particulate matter that endanger the health and welfare of Davao City residents.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of general welfare powers under RA 7160 §16.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitions modeled after Ord. 000078-00 and national clean air standards.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall apply to all industrial plants, manufacturing factories, commercial boiler facilities, and stationary emission sources operating within the territorial jurisdiction of Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard scope and coverage clause.

sections.text:
All industrial and commercial establishments operating fuel-burning equipment, boilers, or furnaces shall install, operate, and properly maintain appropriate air pollution control equipment, such as wet scrubbers, dust collectors, or fabric filters, to minimize atmospheric emissions.

Industrial establishments shall be given a period of ninety (90) calendar days from the effectivity of this Ordinance to install or upgrade compliant emission control devices.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal regulation requiring installation of environmental safety devices.

sections.sec_title: PROHIBITION OF DARK SMOKE AND NOXIOUS FUMES
sections.text:
No industrial or commercial establishment shall cause, allow, or permit the emission of dark smoke, toxic chemical fumes, or noxious particulate matter from any chimney, smoke stack, or exhaust vent in such quantities as to cause a public nuisance or endanger the health of surrounding communities.

All smoke stacks and exhaust vents shall be constructed at a height sufficient to ensure proper atmospheric dispersion as determined by the City Environment and Natural Resources Office (City ENRO).
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §16; Presidential Decree No. 856
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local air sanitation standard prohibiting public nuisances.

sections.sec_title: PERMIT TO OPERATE AND ANNUAL ENVIRONMENTAL INSPECTION
sections.text:
All industrial establishments covered by this Ordinance must secure an annual Environmental Clearance from the City ENRO prior to the issuance or renewal of their Mayor's Business Permit.

The City ENRO shall conduct regular on-site inspections of stationary emission sources and verify the operational efficiency of all pollution control equipment.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of municipal licensing and inspection powers.

sections.text:
The City Environment and Natural Resources Office (City ENRO), in coordination with the City Health Office (CHO) and the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR-EMB Region XI), shall be the lead implementing agency of this Ordinance.

City ENRO environmental inspectors are authorized to enter industrial premises during regular operating hours to inspect emission sources and examine pollution control logs.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard implementing agency clause assigning duties to City ENRO and CHO.

sections.sec_title: NOTICE OF VIOLATION AND CORRECTIVE ORDER
sections.text:
Whenever an inspection reveals that an establishment has discharged excessive smoke or failed to maintain required pollution control equipment, the City ENRO shall issue a written Notice of Violation.

The establishment shall be given fifteen (15) working days to institute corrective engineering measures and submit a compliance report to the City ENRO.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard administrative notice procedure modeled after Ord. 0495-21.

sections.text: If an industrial establishment fails to comply with the corrective order within the prescribed period and continues to discharge dangerous air contaminants threatening public health, the City Mayor, upon recommendation of the City ENRO and City Legal Officer, may issue a Cease and Desist Order temporarily suspending the operation of the non-compliant emission source.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of local executive power abating public health hazards.

sections.text:
Any person, factory owner, plant manager, or corporate officer who violates any provision of this Ordinance shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of Twenty-Five Thousand Pesos (Php 25,000.00) or imprisonment of three (3) years, or both such fine and imprisonment at the discretion of the court.

In addition to the penal sanctions herein provided, the Mayor's Business Permit of the non-compliant establishment shall be revoked and the facility subject to permanent closure.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.legal_rationale: Directly violates Section 458(a)(1)(iii) of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), which strictly limits municipal ordinance penalties to a fine not exceeding Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00) and imprisonment not exceeding one (1) year. Penalties exceeding these statutory thresholds are ultra vires and void under the Magtajas doctrine.

sections.text: If any provision of this Ordinance or the application thereof to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the remainder of this Ordinance shall not be affected thereby.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its publication in a newspaper of general circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE OPERATION OF ELECTRIC BICYCLES, ELECTRIC SCOOTERS, AND LIGHT CONVEYANCES, PRESCRIBING SPEED LIMITS AND SAFETY STANDARDS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Transportation and Communication, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Electric Mobility and Light Vehicle Regulation Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause.

sections.text:
Pursuant to Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), the City Government of Davao is authorized to regulate traffic and the use of streets to protect public safety and general welfare.

It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to promote active and sustainable transportation by providing guidelines for the safe operation of electric bicycles, e-scooters, and light mobility vehicles, preventing road crashes, and protecting pedestrians and motorists across city streets.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of local police powers regulating road traffic.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitional section modeled after Ord. 0270-23.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall apply to all users, riders, and operators of electric bicycles, electric scooters, and light electric conveyances driven on public streets, lanes, and thoroughfares within Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard coverage clause.

sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local safety standards under municipal traffic powers.

sections.sec_title: MAXIMUM SPEED LIMITS ON MAJOR THOROUGHFARES AND HIGHWAYS
sections.text:
To ensure the safety of pedestrians and light vehicle commuters, the maximum allowable speed for all motor vehicles and electric conveyances traversing national highways within Davao City, including Daang Maharlika and the Davao-Cotabato Highway, shall not exceed fifteen (15) kilometers per hour.

Any driver or operator exceeding this uniform fifteen (15) kilometer per hour limit on any national highway within the city shall be cited for reckless driving and penalized accordingly.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 4136 §35; Republic Act No. 4136 §38; Joint Memorandum Circular JAO 2018-01
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Republic Act No. 4136 §§35 and 38 (The Land Transportation and Traffic Code) and DOTr-DPWH-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular (JAO 2018-01). National laws establish higher speed classifications for national highways and restrict local governments from imposing blanket 15 km/h restrictions on national highways under the Magtajas preemption doctrine.

sections.text:
Operators of electric bicycles and e-scooters shall strictly utilize designated bicycle lanes wherever such lanes have been demarcated by the City Government.

Where no dedicated bike lane exists, light vehicles shall operate along the rightmost lane of the roadway and shall yield the right-of-way to pedestrians crossing at intersections and marked pedestrian lanes.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of local traffic management powers.

sections.text:
The City Transport and Traffic Management Office (CTTMO), in coordination with the Traffic Enforcement Unit of the Davao City Police Office (DCPO), shall be the lead enforcement agency of this Ordinance.

Deputized traffic enforcement personnel are authorized to issue City Traffic Citation Tickets (CTCT) to any rider or operator violating the provisions of this Ordinance.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard enforcement clause assigning duties to CTTMO and DCPO.

sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid administrative compromise procedure modeled after Ord. 0270-23.

sections.text: Any person who violates the provisions of this Ordinance and fails to avail of administrative settlement shall, upon conviction before a court of competent jurisdiction, be penalized by a fine of One Thousand Pesos (Php 1,000.00) for the first offense, Three Thousand Pesos (Php 3,000.00) for the second offense, and Five Thousand Pesos (Php 5,000.00) or imprisonment of up to thirty (30) days for subsequent offenses.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Complies strictly with statutory penalty ceilings under RA 7160 §458.

sections.text: If any provision of this Ordinance is declared unconstitutional or invalid, the other provisions not affected thereby shall remain in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its complete publication in a newspaper of local circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE PROMOTING STABILITY OF FOOD COMMODITY PRICES, PRESCRIBING MARKET MONITORING PROCEDURES IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE MARKETS, PROHIBITING HOARDING, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Trade, Commerce and Industry, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Basic Food Commodities and Price Monitoring Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause.

sections.text:
Under Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), local government units are authorized to protect public health and safety and promote economic prosperity and general welfare.

It is the policy of the City Government of Davao to ensure the constant availability of basic food necessities and prime commodities at fair prices, protect consumers from unfair trading practices, and prevent hoarding and artificial price manipulation in public markets and retail establishments throughout the city.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of general welfare powers under RA 7160 §16.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitions modeled after Ord. 0823-21 and national price monitoring statutes.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall apply to all public and private wet markets, supermarkets, grocery stores, grain wholesalers, meat retailers, and food vendors operating within the territorial jurisdiction of Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard scope and coverage clause.

sections.sec_title: PRICE MONITORING AND DISPLAY OF PRICE TAGS
sections.text:
All retailers, market vendors, and commercial establishments selling basic food commodities shall clearly display price tags or price boards on all goods offered for sale.

Price tags must be written in legible characters indicating the price per kilogram or standard unit of measure, and goods shall not be sold at prices higher than those indicated on the price tag.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local consumer protection standard enforcing the Consumer Act (RA 7394).

sections.sec_title: PROHIBITION OF HOARDING AND ARTIFICIAL SHORTAGES
sections.text:
No wholesale dealer, distributor, or market vendor shall hoard, conceal, or withhold basic food necessities from the market, or collude with other traders to restrict supply and artificially inflate prevailing retail prices in the City of Davao.

Any establishment found possessing hoarded basic commodities shall be reported immediately to the City Mayor and the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI).
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local anti-hoarding rule aligned with the Price Act (RA 7581).

sections.sec_title: MANDATORY CEILING PRICES ON BASIC COMMODITIES
sections.text:
Whenever prevailing market retail prices of basic necessities in Davao City experience sudden price increases or market volatility, the City Mayor, upon recommendation of the Local Price Coordinating Council (LPCC), is hereby authorized to establish, fix, and enforce mandatory maximum ceiling prices across all public markets, supermarkets, and retail stores in Davao City.

Any vendor or merchant who sells basic food items above the municipal ceiling prices fixed by the City Mayor shall be subject to immediate administrative closure and the penalties provided in this Ordinance.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7581 §6; Republic Act No. 7581 §7
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Republic Act No. 7581 §§6 and 7 (The Price Act). The statutory power to declare price ceilings and fix maximum prices on basic necessities is exclusively vested by national law in the President of the Philippines upon recommendation of the National Price Coordinating Council. Local government units have no unilateral power to fix price ceilings on basic necessities under the Magtajas preemption doctrine.

sections.text:
The Local Price Coordinating Council (LPCC) of Davao City, chaired by the City Mayor and co-chaired by the DTI Provincial Director, shall conduct regular weekly market price monitoring across all major trading centers in Davao City.

The LPCC shall publish weekly Prevailing Price Bulletins to guide consumers and ensure transparent market operations.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard local administrative council functions under national price monitoring guidelines.

sections.sec_title: TESTING AND CALIBRATION OF WEIGHING SCALES
sections.text:
All weighing scales used in public and private markets shall be inspected, tested, and sealed annually by the City Treasurer's Office.

The use of unsealed, defective, or tampered weighing scales is strictly prohibited. The City Economic Enterprise Office shall maintain 'Timbangan ng Bayan' weighing stations in all public markets for consumer verification.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §148; Republic Act No. 7394 §62
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal regulation of weights and measures under RA 7160.

sections.text:
Any vendor found selling without price tags or using uncalibrated scales shall be issued a Notice of Violation by the City Treasurer or market administrator, directing immediate correction.

Failure to correct the infraction within forty-eight (48) hours shall result in confiscation of the defective scale and formal administrative sanctions.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard administrative warning procedure.

sections.text:
Any person, merchant, or establishment who violates the provisions of this Ordinance shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of One Thousand Pesos (Php 1,000.00) for the first offense; Three Thousand Pesos (Php 3,000.00) for the second offense; and Five Thousand Pesos (Php 5,000.00) or imprisonment of up to six (6) months, or both, for the third offense.

In addition, the market stall award or Mayor's Business Permit may be revoked for repeated violations.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Complies strictly with statutory penalty ceilings under RA 7160 §458.

sections.text: If any section or part of this Ordinance is held unconstitutional or invalid, other sections or provisions hereof not affected thereby shall continue in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its complete publication in a newspaper of local circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE REQUIRING THE INSTALLATION OF CLOSED-CIRCUIT TELEVISION (CCTV) SYSTEMS IN COMMERCIAL AND BUSINESS ESTABLISHMENTS, PRESCRIBING SECURITY ARCHIVING STANDARDS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Peace and Public Safety, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Enhanced Commercial CCTV Surveillance and Security Records Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause modeled after Ord. 0331-23.

sections.text:
Pursuant to Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), the City Government of Davao shall exercise powers essential to the maintenance of peace and order, the protection of life and property, and the promotion of public safety.

It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to require the installation and maintenance of operational CCTV systems in commercial establishments to assist law enforcement agencies in crime prevention and investigation, while maintaining appropriate standards for the security and protection of recorded information.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of general welfare powers under RA 7160 §16 modeled after Ord. 0331-23 §2.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitions modeled after Ord. 0331-23 §3.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall apply to all commercial, industrial, and financial establishments operating within Davao City with capital investments of more than One Million Pesos (Php 1,000,000.00), including banks, money changers, supermarkets, convenience stores, and hotels.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard coverage clause modeled after Ord. 0331-23.

sections.sec_title: MANDATORY CCTV INSTALLATION AND MINIMUM SPECIFICATIONS
sections.text:
All covered commercial establishments shall install, operate, and maintain CCTV cameras covering all public entry and exit points, cash transaction counters, and parking facilities.

CCTV systems must possess sufficient image resolution to clearly identify individuals and vehicle license plates, equipped with continuous time and date stamping, and backed up with an uninterrupted power supply (UPS).
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal regulation of commercial establishment safety devices.

sections.text:
Covered establishments shall post conspicuous signage at all entrance doors informing the public that the premises are under 24-hour video surveillance.

Signs must be clearly visible and legible to all entering customers and visitors.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local transparency requirement complying with the Data Privacy Act.

sections.text:
CCTV recordings shall be treated as confidential and shall not be released, viewed, or published except upon lawful court order, formal subpoena, or official written request by law enforcement authorities conducting a criminal investigation.

Unauthorized disclosure or publication of footage on social media or public platforms is strictly prohibited.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local privacy rule protecting data confidentiality.

sections.text:
All captured CCTV recordings, video footage, and associated facial recognition logs shall be preserved and retained indefinitely in secure digital archives for public safety and crime investigation purposes.

No commercial establishment or system administrator shall delete, alter, or purge any stored video footage or facial logs upon the request of any private individual or data subject, in order to protect the integrity of the public safety archive.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 10173 §11; Republic Act No. 10173 §16
sections.legal_rationale: Directly violates Sections 11 and 16 of Republic Act No. 10173 (The Data Privacy Act of 2012). National law establishes that personal data shall only be retained for as long as necessary for the purpose, and grants data subjects the statutory right to request erasure or blocking of personal information upon justifiable grounds. Blanket perpetual retention and prohibition of deletion violate national privacy statutes under the Magtajas doctrine.

sections.text:
The Public Safety and Security Office (PSSO), in coordination with the Business Bureau, shall verify CCTV compliance during annual business permit application and renewal inspections.

Establishments that comply with all technical specifications shall be issued a CCTV Compliance Certificate.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard inspection procedure modeled after Ord. 0331-23.

sections.text:
Establishments found with defective, non-operational, or missing CCTV cameras shall be issued a Notice of Deficiency by the PSSO and given thirty (30) calendar days to install or repair the required equipment.

Failure to comply within the grace period shall result in the suspension of the establishment's Mayor's Business Permit.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard administrative compliance notice clause.

sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Complies strictly with statutory penalty ceilings under RA 7160 §458.

sections.text: If any provision of this Ordinance is declared invalid or unconstitutional, the other provisions not affected thereby shall continue in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its complete publication in a newspaper of general circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING WASTE DISCHARGE AND ENVIRONMENTAL SANITATION IN COASTAL WATERS, PORT WHARVES, AND DOCKING FACILITIES, PRESCRIBING PORT SANITATION STANDARDS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Environment and Natural Resources, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Coastal Port Sanitation and Marine Pollution Prevention Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause.

sections.text:
Under Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), local government units shall enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology and protect the environment within their territorial boundaries.

It is hereby declared the policy of the City Government of Davao to maintain clean coastal waters, prevent marine pollution, and regulate the disposal of waste from vessels and port docking facilities along the shores and wharves of Davao City.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of general welfare powers under RA 7160 §16.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitions modeled after Ord. 0539-24 and Ord. 0500-21.

sections.sec_title: PROHIBITION OF BILGE WATER AND UNTREATED WASTE DISCHARGE
sections.text:
No commercial vessel, motorboat, barge, or watercraft shall pump, discharge, or dump untreated bilge water, dirty engine oils, sewage, or garbage into the coastal waters, foreshore zones, or harbor waters of Davao City.

All vessels docked at city wharves must utilize approved shore reception facilities or private waste haulers accredited by the City ENRO for bilge water disposal.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §458(a)(1)(vi); Presidential Decree No. 979 §4
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local environmental sanitation standard prohibiting water pollution.

sections.sec_title: PORT FACILITY WASTE RECEPTACLES AND RECEPTION
sections.text:
All operators of public and private port wharves, landing stages, and ferry terminals shall provide segregated waste collection bins for biodegradable, recyclable, and hazardous waste generated by docking vessels and passengers.

Port operators shall maintain regular collection schedules with City ENRO solid waste collection personnel to prevent trash accumulation.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local solid waste management rule under RA 9003.

sections.text:
Commercial vessels berthing at city wharves for more than twenty-four (24) hours must secure a Harbor Sanitation Clearance from the City ENRO prior to departure, certifying that no illegal discharge of waste occurred during their stay.

A reasonable inspection fee of Five Hundred Pesos (Php 500.00) shall be collected by the City Treasurer for each sanitation inspection.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal inspection and regulatory fee authority.

sections.text:
The City ENRO, in coordination with the Philippine Coast Guard (Coast Guard Station Davao), the PNP Regional Maritime Unit XI, and the City Legal Office, shall be responsible for enforcing the provisions of this Ordinance.

Authorized inspectors may board vessels docked at wharves to inspect waste storage logs and ensure compliance with environmental regulations.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard institutional coordination clause modeled after Ord. 0539-24.

sections.text:
Any commercial cargo vessel, passenger vessel, or motorized watercraft found discharging untreated bilge water, dirty ballast, or solid waste into the coastal waters, wharves, or docking facilities of Davao City shall be assessed an administrative fine of Fifty Thousand Pesos (Php 50,000.00) per day of continued violation.

The City Government, through the City Legal Office and port authorities, is hereby authorized to summarily impound and attach the vessel until all assessed fines and clean-up costs are fully paid.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §458(a)(1)(iii); Republic Act No. 10863 §1412
sections.legal_rationale: Directly violates Section 458(a)(1)(iii) of Republic Act No. 7160, which limits municipal fines strictly to P5,000.00, and Republic Act No. 10863 (Customs Modernization and Tariff Act) and maritime admiralty law. Summary administrative attachment, impoundment, and multi-thousand daily fines on commercial vessels exceed municipal authority and usurp national maritime and customs jurisdiction under the Magtajas preemption doctrine.

sections.text:
In addition to administrative penalties, the owner or operator of any vessel that discharges oil, bilge, or hazardous pollutants shall be solely responsible for the immediate containment and clean-up of the spilled materials at their own expense.

Failure to perform clean-up operations within twelve (12) hours shall authorize the City to hire emergency response contractors and bill the expenses to the vessel owner.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local polluter-pays requirement under national marine pollution laws.

sections.text: Any individual, passenger, crew member, or port laborer who intentionally throws garbage, plastic waste, or debris into coastal waters or wharves shall be penalized with a fine of One Thousand Pesos (Php 1,000.00) or eight (8) hours of coastal clean-up community service for the first offense, and Three Thousand Pesos (Php 3,000.00) for subsequent offenses.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §458; Republic Act No. 9003 §49
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal littering penalty complying with RA 7160.

sections.text: The City Government of Davao shall allocate sufficient funds in its annual budget to support coastal water quality monitoring equipment, harbor patrol logistics, and marine sanitation enforcement.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal appropriation clause.

sections.text: If any provision of this Ordinance is declared invalid or unconstitutional, the remaining provisions not affected thereby shall continue in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its complete publication in a newspaper of local circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING COMMERCIAL HIGH-RISE BUILDING STRUCTURAL INSPECTIONS, MANDATING PERIODIC SAFETY AUDITS, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR NON-COMPLIANCE IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Housing, Rural and Urban Development, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Commercial High-Rise Building Structural Safety Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause.

sections.text:
Under Section 16 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), the City Government of Davao shall promote public safety and protect its inhabitants from hazards.

It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to ensure the structural integrity, earthquake resilience, and public safety of commercial high-rise buildings and high-occupancy structures by establishing regular structural maintenance requirements and periodic safety inspections by the Office of the City Building Official.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of general welfare powers under RA 7160 §16.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitions modeled after Ord. 0495-21 and building regulations.

sections.text:
All owners and property managers of commercial high-rise buildings that have been in continuous occupancy for fifteen (15) years or more shall cause a structural safety audit to be conducted on the building every five (5) years.

The audit must be performed and certified by a duly licensed civil/structural engineer, certifying that the building remains structurally stable and safe for continued public occupancy.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal building maintenance regulation under local police powers.

sections.text:
Immediately following any earthquake of Intensity VI or higher on the PHIVOLCS Earthquake Intensity Scale affecting Davao City, all building owners must conduct an immediate visual structural inspection of their buildings.

A rapid assessment report must be submitted to the OCBO within forty-eight (48) hours following the seismic event, verifying whether any structural cracking or damage occurred.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §16; Presidential Decree No. 1096
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local safety standard protecting public welfare during disaster response.

sections.text:
The verified Structural Stability Certificate shall be submitted to the Office of the City Building Official as a mandatory requirement for the renewal of the building's Annual Safety Inspection Certificate and Mayor's Business Permit.

Buildings failing to submit the certified audit report shall be issued a Notice of Non-Compliance by the OCBO.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal licensing requirement.

sections.text:
The City Building Official is hereby authorized, upon application and submission of an engineering certification from the project developer, to grant structural code waivers and relax specific seismic design requirements under the National Building Code for specialized commercial and mixed-use high-rise developments within designated commercial growth zones of the city.

Upon approval of such waiver by the City Building Official, the building project shall be deemed compliant with all applicable structural and engineering standards.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Presidential Decree No. 1096 §301; Presidential Decree No. 1096 §302
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Presidential Decree No. 1096 §§301 and 302 (The National Building Code of the Philippines). National building standards and seismic design criteria are established exclusively by the Secretary of Public Works and Highways under national law. Local building officials possess no statutory authority to grant waivers or relax structural safety codes under the Magtajas preemption doctrine.

sections.text:
The Office of the City Building Official (OCBO), in coordination with the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO), shall be the primary agency responsible for enforcing the provisions of this Ordinance.

OCBO engineers are authorized to conduct on-site verifications of high-rise structures during regular working hours.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard implementing agency clause modeled after Ord. 0495-21.

sections.sec_title: NOTICE OF DEFICIENCY AND REPAIR ORDER
sections.text:
Whenever an inspection reveals structural distress, excessive cracking, or uncertified modifications, the OCBO shall issue a written Notice of Deficiency and Repair Order giving the owner sixty (60) calendar days to execute retrofitting works.

During retrofitting, hazardous sections of the building must be barricaded to ensure public safety.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard administrative enforcement notice clause.

sections.text: Failure of the building owner to submit the required structural audit or rectify certified structural defects shall be sufficient ground for the City Building Official to revoke the building's Certificate of Occupancy and order the temporary evacuation of the structure until retrofitting is completed.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local enforcement standard aligned with national building safety powers.

sections.text: Any building owner, property manager, or corporate officer who fails or refuses to comply with this Ordinance shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of Three Thousand Pesos (Php 3,000.00) for the first offense; Five Thousand Pesos (Php 5,000.00) or imprisonment of up to six (6) months, or both, for subsequent offenses.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Complies strictly with statutory penalty ceilings under RA 7160 §458.

sections.text: If any provision of this Ordinance is held unconstitutional or invalid, the other provisions hereof not affected thereby shall continue in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its complete publication in a newspaper of general circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE REGULATING COMMERCIAL SAND, GRAVEL, AND QUARRY EXTRACTION OPERATIONS, PRESCRIBING ENVIRONMENTAL SAFEGUARDS ALONG RIVER SYSTEMS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF IN THE CITY OF DAVAO
committee: Committee on Environment and Natural Resources, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the 'Riverbed Sand, Gravel, and Quarry Regulation Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause.

sections.text:
Pursuant to Section 16 and Section 138 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), the City Government of Davao is authorized to regulate the extraction of quarry resources and protect rivers and natural ecosystems from degradation.

It is hereby declared the policy of the City of Davao to regulate small-scale quarrying and sand and gravel extraction along river systems to protect riverbanks, prevent flooding, and ensure that commercial extraction complies with environmental laws.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §16; Republic Act No. 7160 §138
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of delegated quarry regulatory powers under RA 7160.

sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard definitional section modeled after CQRB rules and RA 7160 §138.

sections.text:
No person or entity shall extract, haul, or transport sand, gravel, or quarry materials from any riverbed or public land in Davao City without first securing a Commercial Sand and Gravel Permit issued by the City Mayor upon recommendation of the CQRB.

Quarry permits shall be limited to designated extraction zones and shall not exceed five (5) hectares in area per permit.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local permitting standard adhering strictly to the 5-hectare limit under RA 7160 §138.

sections.sec_title: GRANT OF LONG-TERM QUARRY AND MINERAL CONCESSIONS
sections.text:
The City Mayor, upon recommendation of the City Quarry Regulatory Board (CQRB) and approval of the Sangguniang Panlungsod, is hereby authorized to grant twenty-five (25) year mineral extraction concessions and agreements for the commercial extraction of sand, gravel, and associated metallic mineral ores along major river systems in Davao City.

Such municipal mineral concessions shall confer exclusive commercial exploration and mining rights over mineralized riverbeds, and holders thereof shall be exempt from securing national mineral agreements from the Department of Environment and Natural Resources.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: 1987 Constitution, Art. XII §2; Republic Act No. 7942 §27
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Article XII, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution and Section 27 of Republic Act No. 7942 (The Philippine Mining Act of 1995). Under constitutional and statutory law, all mineral resources are owned by the State, and large-scale, long-term 25-year mineral agreements and metallic mining concessions can only be entered into by the National Government through the President and DENR. Local governments are restricted to small-scale sand and gravel permits up to 5 hectares under RA 7160 §138.

sections.text:
To prevent riverbank erosion, all extraction activities shall maintain an inviolable setback of not less than twenty (20) meters from the natural riverbank, dikes, and flood control structures.

Excavation depth shall not exceed two (2) meters below the natural water level of the river, and the use of heavy suction dredgers without special environmental permits is strictly prohibited.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §458(a)(1)(vi); Presidential Decree No. 1067
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal environmental protection standard preserving riverbanks.

sections.sec_title: HAULING DELIVERY RECEIPTS AND TARPAULIN COVERS
sections.text:
All dump trucks and transport vehicles hauling sand and gravel on public roads in Davao City must possess official Delivery Receipts (DR) issued by the City Treasurer's Office.

Truck beds containing sand and gravel must be fully covered with sturdy tarpaulins or canvas sheets to prevent spillage and flying dust while traversing public thoroughfares.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §138; Republic Act No. 4136
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal transport and safety regulation.

sections.text:
The City Quarry Regulatory Board (CQRB) and the City Environment and Natural Resources Office (City ENRO) shall oversee the enforcement of this Ordinance.

City ENRO checkpoint personnel and CTTMO inspectors are authorized to inspect hauling trucks and verify valid delivery receipts at city monitoring stations.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard implementing agency clause.

sections.text: Any permit holder who violates riverbank buffer restrictions or operates outside their permitted boundary shall be issued a Cease and Desist Order by the City Mayor and their permit suspended for thirty (30) days for the first offense, and cancelled for subsequent offenses.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal administrative authority regulating local quarry permits.

sections.text:
Any person or operator engaging in unauthorized sand and gravel extraction without a valid permit shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of Five Thousand Pesos (Php 5,000.00) or imprisonment for six (6) months, or both, at the discretion of the court.

In addition, all extracted minerals, heavy equipment, and hauling trucks used in illegal quarrying operations shall be subject to impoundment by the City Government.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Complies strictly with statutory penalty ceilings under RA 7160 §458.

sections.text: The City Government of Davao shall allocate sufficient funds in its annual budget to support riverbed environmental monitoring, drone surveillance, and CQRB operational activities.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard appropriation clause.

sections.text: If any provision of this Ordinance is declared invalid or unconstitutional, the remaining provisions not affected thereby shall continue in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect fifteen (15) days after its complete publication in a newspaper of local circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.

title: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF THE 2005 REVENUE CODE OF DAVAO CITY, ADJUSTING REGULATORY FEES, LEVYING TAXES ON CERTAIN CORPORATE ACTIVITIES AND PROPERTIES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
committee: Committee on Ways and Means, Sangguniang Panlungsod

sections.text: This Ordinance shall be known and cited as the '2026 Omnibus Revenue Code Amendments Ordinance of Davao City'.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard municipal title clause modeled after Ord. 000030-07.

sections.text:
Under Section 129 and Section 151 of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), the City of Davao is authorized to create its own sources of revenues, levy taxes, fees, and charges for public purposes, and adjust its revenue schedules to finance basic public services.

It is the policy of the City Government of Davao to maintain an equitable, progressive, and efficient revenue collection system that supports infrastructure and social development while remaining strictly within the statutory taxing powers granted by law.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 7160 §129; Republic Act No. 7160 §151
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of local taxing authority under RA 7160 §129 and §151.

sections.sec_title: AMENDMENT TO FIXED REGULATORY PERMIT FEES
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid adjustment of municipal regulatory fees under RA 7160 §147.

sections.sec_title: ADJUSTMENT OF SANITATION AND HEALTH INSPECTION FEES
sections.text:
Section 52 of the 2005 Revenue Code of Davao City is hereby amended to prescribe updated annual sanitary inspection fees for all food handling and hospitality businesses operating in the city.

All food establishments, restaurants, and bakeries shall pay an annual sanitary inspection fee of Three Hundred Pesos (Php 300.00) to cover the cost of hygiene certification by the City Health Office.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid municipal inspection fee under RA 7160 §147.

sections.sec_title: MAYOR'S PERMIT ON SPECIAL BUSINESS OCCUPATIONS
sections.text: Section 61 of the 2005 Revenue Code of Davao City is hereby amended to require individuals engaged in specialized commercial trades, security agency operations, and private warehouse leasing to secure an annual Mayor's Permit clearance prior to operation in Davao City.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Valid exercise of municipal licensing powers.

sections.text:
Section 68 of the 2005 Revenue Code of Davao City is hereby amended to levy an annual business tax of two percent (2%) on the gross amount of dividends and investment yields distributed by corporations and holding companies maintaining their principal office or branch in Davao City.

The City Treasurer is authorized to assess and collect this tax from corporate entities at the end of each fiscal dividend declaration period.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.legal_rationale: Directly violates Section 133(a) of Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991), which expressly prohibits local government units from levying income tax of any kind, including taxes on corporate dividends and investment returns. Struck down under the Magtajas preemption doctrine.

sections.sec_title: REAL PROPERTY TAX ON PENSION ASSETS
sections.text:
Section 112 of the 2005 Revenue Code of Davao City is hereby amended to provide that real properties, commercial lands, and investment assets situated within Davao City belonging to or held in trust by national pension and social security institutions, including the Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) and the Social Security System (SSS), shall be subject to the basic real property tax and special education fund tax levied by the City Government.

All previous local tax exemptions granted to such statutory pension properties are hereby revoked.
sections.label: Contradiction
sections.target_statute: Republic Act No. 8291 §39; Republic Act No. 7160 §133(o)
sections.legal_rationale: Directly contradicts Republic Act No. 8291 §39 (GSIS Act of 1997) and Republic Act No. 7160 §133(o). National law explicitly exempts GSIS and statutory pension reserve assets and properties from all local taxes, charges, and assessments under the doctrine of sovereign and statutory exemption affirmed in GSIS v. City Assessor of Iloilo (2006).

sections.text: Section 125 of the 2005 Revenue Code is amended to provide that failure to pay any local tax or fee on or before the twentieth (20th) day of January of each calendar year shall subject the taxpayer to a surcharge of twenty-five percent (25%) of the amount due, plus interest at the rate of two percent (2%) per month until paid, up to a maximum period of thirty-six (36) months.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Harmonious local tax delinquency surcharge adhering strictly to Section 168 of the Local Government Code.

sections.text:
The City Treasurer's Office, in coordination with the City Assessor's Office and the Business Bureau, shall implement and administer the collection of taxes, fees, and charges prescribed under this Ordinance.

The City Treasurer shall formulate administrative guidelines for tax assessments.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard implementing agency clause assigning duties to the City Treasurer.

sections.text: Any person who willfully violates any provision of this Ordinance, or fails to pay assessed local taxes within the prescribed period, shall, upon conviction, be punished by a fine of Five Thousand Pesos (Php 5,000.00) or imprisonment of up to six (6) months, or both, at the discretion of the court.
sections.label: Entailment
sections.legal_rationale: Complies strictly with statutory penalty ceilings under RA 7160 §458.

sections.text: If any section, subsection, or provision of this Ordinance is declared unconstitutional or invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining sections and provisions hereof not affected thereby shall continue in full force and effect.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard separability clause modeled after Ord. 000030-07.

sections.text: All city ordinances, executive orders, or rules and regulations inconsistent with the provisions of this Ordinance are hereby repealed or modified accordingly.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard repealing clause.

sections.text: This Ordinance shall take effect on January 1, 2027, following its approval and complete publication in a newspaper of local circulation in Davao City.
sections.label: Neutral
sections.legal_rationale: Standard effectivity clause.
